meta.unit: the package-wide bytes canon (Codex round 7): every RPC-decoded quantity passes checkCanonicalQuantity, every variable-length payload passes checkCanonicalData, the mined-log wire shape is presence-tracked, and a null eth_getLogs result is refused — an empty quantity or payload can never become a value THROUGH ANY PATH in internal/chain
meta.purpose: Task 9 wave 8 brief's mutation requirement: one mutant per NEW gate arm, with per-path isolation visible in the kill lists — W8M1 (eth_blockNumber, the F1 binding path), W8M2/W8M3/W8M4 (the three log quantity wrappers, W8M2 being the F2 binding path), W8M5 (the log data canon application), W8M6 (the data canon's shared empty arm), W8M7 (the null-window gate), W8M8/W8M9 (presence devolving to zero for logIndex/blockNumber, the pinned decoder's own leniency restored faithfully), W8M10 (eth_chainId), W8M11/W8M12 (tx input canon and presence). Run through the wave-16 committed applier (.superpowers/sdd/wave16-mutations/mutate.py): exactly-one-occurrence asserted per edit, byte-level backups, in-memory restores verified byte-identical. chain.go is a uniform-CRLF working copy (CR count == line count, verified), so every multi-line pattern embeds \r\n explicitly.
design_notes: EVERY MUTANT LIVES IN A WAVE-8 GATE — the endpointClient overrides' canon calls, the per-field strict wrappers, checkCanonicalData's empty arm, validateReportedLog's presence arms and FilterLogs' null gate. The fake-seam tests are STRUCTURALLY BLIND to all twelve by design: fakeRPC scripts post-decode VALUES (types.Log slices, uint64 heights, big.Int chain ids), so every kill must come from the raw-JSON layer (chain_rawjson_test.go), which drives the REAL stack Dial -> rpc.Client -> endpointClient overrides -> wrappers -> gates. The kill lists are the proof that layer reaches every new gate.

PER-PATH ISOLATION IS THE POINT OF THE MATRIX SHAPE: W8M1's kill list must be purely eth_blockNumber-side, W8M2's purely logIndex-side, W8M3's purely log-blockNumber-side, W8M4's purely transactionIndex-side, W8M5's purely log-data-side, W8M10's purely chainId-side, W8M11/12's purely tx-input-side. A kill leaking across paths would mean one test is doing another gate's work and the per-field independence claim is false.

W8M1 AND W8M2 ARE THE BRIEF'S BINDING PAIR (property: an empty quantity can never become a value THROUGH THIS PATH) AND ARE BEHAVIORAL KILLS: under W8M1 the empty eth_blockNumber read SUCCEEDS as height 0 from the malformed primary (no rotation — the walker-starving F1 shape) and the null read succeeds as height 0 too; under W8M2 the empty-logIndex window SUCCEEDS and hands downstream a present index zero as the raw-log identity/order (the F2 persistence-corruption shape). The binding regressions assert error-plus-rotation-plus-landing, so both die on every leg. W8M5 and W8M11 are behavioral the same way for the data canon: hexutil.Bytes lenient-ACCEPTS "" (as the empty payload) and uppercase (as the bytes), so with the gate bypassed those reads SUCCEED where the matrix asserts refusal.

W8M10 IS BEHAVIORAL VIA THE WANT-ZERO ARM: for want 10 the minted chain id 0 still fails VerifyChainID's equality (a name-level observable), but the matrix carries VerifyChainID(ctx, 0) against a scripted "" — under the mutant that call PASSES (0 == 0), which is precisely the one-layer-up leniency dependence the gate exists to remove.

W8M6 AND W8M12 ARE MESSAGE-LEVEL KILLS, disclosed: under W8M6 the empty payload is still refused by the data canon's next arm (the 0x-prefix check), and under W8M12 an omitted input is still refused by the pinned transaction decoder's own required-field list ('missing required field input in transaction') — rotation is identical either way and the observable is the violation's NAME. That name is the property: a gate whose rejections silently devolve to the library's own strictness profile is one library upgrade away from re-admitting the class, and "" -> empty IS that library's current profile one form over (the exact wave-7 argument, restated for data).

W8M8 AND W8M9 RESTORE THE PINNED DECODER'S ABSENCE LENIENCY FAITHFULLY, each with TWO edits: the presence arm stops naming the absence AND the conversion defaults the absent field to zero — exactly what gen_log_json.go does today (an omitted logIndex IS index 0, an omitted blockNumber IS height 0, audit-executed). A single-edit deletion of just the presence arm would nil-panic at the conversion — a kill, but of a strawman; the two-edit form is the honest pre-wave-8 behavior.

MUTANT COMPILABILITY by construction: W8M1/W8M10 leave `raw` consumed by the hexutil decode below; W8M2-5/W8M11 leave a bare delegation to the hexutil decoder; W8M6 deletes an arm whose operand s remains used by later arms; W8M7 deletes a scoped if-statement (bytes package still used by TransactionByHash); W8M8/W8M9 replace the conversion expression with a guarded closure; W8M12 leaves probe consumed via probe.BlockNumber at the return.

SOLVENT_LIVE_RPC_TESTS stays UNSET for every mutation run (no public-endpoint hammering in loops; the raw-JSON servers are local httptest instances). TEST_DATABASE_URL points at solvent_t9w1, never at the backfill daemon's DB solvent.
